messages:
Tara: Thinking aloud — we need a fast-path migration lane for enterprise customers who require instant pinning + rollback guarantees during catalog migrations. Proposal: an "enterprise escape hatch" that lets us pin a tenant to a legacy model for up to 30 days, with an ops-backed rollback if canary shows regression. Thoughts?
Sanjay: +1 to the idea. main risks: capacity fragmentation and SLA exposure. How do we prevent pin abuse?
Tara: Good point. controls: 1) approval by Solutions + Sales for each pin, 2) hard TTL (30d), 3) metric gating to auto-expire earlier if stable canary meets criteria.
Ella: For approval flow, we should require a short risk form from Solutions listing customer SLOs, compliance reasons, and expected qps. That will help capacity planning.
Priya: From Sales — customers asking for this already. We should make the onboarding path explicit and bill for reserved capacity if >100qps sustained.
Oliver: On the model side, we need launch criteria for the migration. Proposed canary rules: run 48h at min 5k requests, compare NLU eval set with threshold: delta <= 0.5% on top-1 accuracy and latency P99 <= 220ms on dedicated pool. If fail, auto-fallback to pinned model.
Tara: That reads like a good baseline. Also add quality-monitoring: alerts for hallucination rate increase >0.7% on sampled prompts.
Sanjay: Ops question — how will the rollback be executed? manual ops runbook or automated?
Ella: Prefer automated rollback with human-in-the-loop: if canary fails gating, deploy-bot posts trigger, ops reviews within 30m, otherwise auto-rollback after 2h. Keeps safety while reducing toil.
deploy-bot: FYI — draft hook: 
```
canary_policy: {
  duration: "48h",
  min_samples: 5000,
  metrics: ["top1_accuracy_delta","p99_latency","hallucination_rate"],
  thresholds: {"top1_accuracy_delta":0.5,"p99_latency":220,"hallucination_rate":0.7}
}
rollback: {auto_after_hours:2, notify: ["ops","solutions","sales"]}
```
Priya: We need comms wording for customers: "temporary pin available for 30 days to ensure compliance. We will recommend migration path and shared benchmark results." Legal to review but okay to draft.
Oliver: One extra thing — compatibility shim for client SDKs: if new model changes tokenization/embeddings, provide a compat adapter for 30d so customers don't get silent vector drift.
Tara: Next steps: (1) draft the approval form (Ella), (2) implement canary_policy hook and runbook (Sanjay + Oliver), (3) draft customer comms + billing terms (Priya), (4) legal review. Target: pilot with 2 customers in 6 weeks. Assignments?
Ella: Taking the approval form. Will sync with Solutions next Tue.
Sanjay: I'll own the runbook and the ops automation.
Oliver: I'll wire the metric checks into Optimize and provide a test harness.
Priya: I'll pick two pilot customers and draft comms + pricing.
Tara: Perfect. I'll create a brief RFC and add to roadmap intake. :thumbsup:
